ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, shareholders above 25%, and immediate family members must be screened against the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions Lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Republic of Korea's financial sanctions designations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and KoFIU guidance. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, including legislative, executive, judicial, military, and state-owned-enterprise officials, based on public official registers, adverse media, corporate registry data, and sanctions file checks. Matching alerts must be escalated to the compliance committee, source-of-wealth documented, and records retained for at least five years after termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-RO) for commercial registration name search, supplemented by the National Tax Service HomeTax system for business registration tax identification purposes
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be in Hangul; a foreign-language name may be registered if the Articles of Incorporation contain the Hangul transcription and the original foreign name is stated in a parallel column. The four-tier convention is: primary Hangul name, English romanized or foreign equivalent, business-scope descriptive element, and legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. The registry applies sound and visual similarity checks to prevent deceptively identical or misleading names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, obtain and preserve the Registrar's written refusal. Submit a curative objection within seven calendar days at the same commercial registry, attaching the corrected Hangul or English name, industry scope explanation, and a side-by-side comparison with the conflicting name. If refused again, file an immediate appeal to the competent District Court under the Commercial Registration Rules within three weeks, submitting the refusal notice, amended name application, evidence of prior use, and legal memoranda distinguishing phonetic or visual similarity. During appeal, run a fresh name search and prepare an alternative name to avoid missed reservation windows.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korea permits a registered office to be supplied by a serviced office or virtual office only if it is a tangible address under a genuine lease or service agreement, and it is not a mere post office box. The National Tax Service and commercial banks will normally reject a mailbox-only arrangement for the logistics technology SaaS sector because the entity cannot demonstrate an actual business establishment, payroll, IT infrastructure, or invoicing functions. A serviced office with dedicated meeting space, signage, power, internet, and mail handling is low-risk; a shared bench model is high-risk and invites VAT denial, bank refusal, and NTS field audit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease contract, occupancy proof, on-site signboard, employees or outsourced staff contracts, servers or laptops, telematics dashboards, corporate telephone number, utility or internet bills, business tax invoices, and dispatch operation records. Quantified risk of unannounced municipal tax or National Tax Service inspection: 5-10% for a fully equipped physical office; 25-35% for a virtual or serviced-address-only arrangement; up to 60% for a mailbox-only address combined with a foreign-owned parent, low paid-in capital, and no VAT filing records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Part II, Chapter VII, Articles 287-2 through 287-74 governing the Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), Article 317 on Registration of Incorporation, and Article 22 on the location of the registered office; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 4 through 6 for foreign investment notification; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inbound capital remittance declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registration Office having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office in the Republic of Korea (for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office); subsequent taxpayer registration with the competent National Tax Service district office and municipal Si/Gun/Gu revenue office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company filed in the Korean commercial registry under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, together with the supporting articles of incorporation, contribution payment evidence and statutory appointment consents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; the articles may validly fix capital as low as KRW 1. No blocked escrow account is required by Korean company law. For a non-resident foreign investor, the subscribed contribution must be remitted through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, and the bank's deposit confirmation or balance certificate naming the proposed company or the incorporator's dedicated subscription account must be preserved as evidence of full payment-in before court registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS, AS APPLICABLE, OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY), REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ON INCORPORATION MATTERS. WHEREAS, the Articles of Incorporation of Yuhang Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) (the Company) have been prepared in the Korean language and executed by the incorporators in accordance with Articles 287-3 and 287-4 of the Commercial Act; and WHEREAS, the incorporators have subscribed for the entire capital contribution units in the amount of KRW [insert amount] and have made full payment of the cash contributions, with payment compliance to be evidenced by a deposit confirmation of a licensed Korean commercial bank; and WHEREAS, it is necessary to authorize the initial operations of the Company, including the selection of the registered office, the opening of bank accounts, the appointment of initial statutory officers, and the filing of the incorporation registration with the competent District Court Registry; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, effective as of the date of this resolution, as follows: 1. Capital Subscription and Confirmation. The subscription of the total issued capital contribution units of KRW [insert amount] is ratified and confirmed. The directors are directed to maintain the statutory member register and contribution ledger, and to exercise all powers necessary to complete the registration of the paid-in capital with the court. 2. Registered Office. The registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be located at [insert complete address], Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the office lease, obtain the lessor's consent, and file the address with the court registry and the tax authority. 3. Banking Authorization. The Representative Director, the Director of Operations, and the Chief Financial Officer, or any two of them acting jointly, are authorized to open bank accounts in the Company's name, including operating, foreign currency, and settlement accounts; to sign account mandates and electronic banking agreements; to initiate wire transfers; and to provide bankers with certified extracts of this resolution and the corporate seal certificate. All disbursements above USD 10,000 or equivalent require dual authorization. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following appointments are made and each appointee accepts the respective office: (a) Person A as Representative Director; (b) Person B as Director of Operations; and (c) Person C as Auditor, if required by the number of equity interest holders or by the Articles. Each officer shall exercise the powers provided by law, discharge all duties under the Commercial Act, and act in accordance with the fiduciary standards imposed by the Republic of Korea. 5. Filing and Government Procedures. The Representative Director and the law firm handling the incorporation are authorized to execute and file all registration forms, powers of attorney, foreign investment reports, tax registrations, licenses, and other documents required to commence business, and to pay all official fees. 6. General Authority and Reliance. This resolution constitutes a valid corporate act of the Company and may be relied upon by the District Court Registration Office, banks, notaries, KOTRA, and the National Tax Service as conclusive evidence of the approvals contained herein. Officers may delegate administrative tasks to the incorporation agent, but no delegation shall limit the duties of the officers under the Commercial Act. ADOPTED on [date] by unanimous written consent of the incorporators, directors, and members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Notification and Inbound Capital Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest KOREA (Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency Korea Investment Support Center) and/or a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank designated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application, each non-resident investor must complete a foreign investment report under Article 6 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and submit a foreign exchange declaration to the bank receiving the remitted capital. The report should be filed through Invest KOREA's online foreign investment support system or at a designated Korean bank window with foreign exchange dealing authority. The investor must specify the newly formed Yuhan Hoesa, the number of equity interests to be subscribed, the exact purpose of investment, the projected capital amount, and the proposed foreign ownership percentage. The report should be accepted before the subscription payment is remitted, and afterward KOTRA will issue a certificate of foreign investment report that the bank and the court registry will use. If the investor is a corporate entity, its certificate of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the investment, and passport or registered officer identification must be apostilled or legalized; every foreign-language document must be accompanied by a Korean translation.
required_dossiers: Completed foreign investment report form (Invest KOREA format)
Passport or corporate identification of the foreign investor
Certificate of incorporation and good standing certificate of the corporate investor
Board resolution of the corporate investor authorizing the Korean investment
Power of attorney appointing the local filing agent
Bank foreign exchange declaration form and remittance instruction schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Invest KOREA or the foreign exchange bank issues a supplementary request, the applicant must submit corrected or translated documents within five business days. If the report is rejected because of incomplete beneficiary or purpose codes, revise the foreign exchange classification and refile through the same bank window; a late or corrected report does not invalidate the incorporation but may delay the bank's issuance of the contribution deposit confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public at the law office or independent notary office; legal counsel admitted in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel will draft the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in conformity with Articles 287-3 and 287-4 of the Commercial Act. The articles must state the company name, the exact business purpose aligned with ISIC 6201 and including fleet route optimization software, real-time telematics SaaS, data processing, and related technology services; the registered office address; the total capital contribution amount and number of membership interests allocated to each incorporator; the kind and monetary value of each contribution; the names and resident registration data of the directors and auditor; the fiscal year; and any special contribution or transfer restrictions. Each incorporator shall sign and seal the articles. Where the Registry, the bank, or the foreign investor requires additional authentication, the articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public. Foreign investor signatures on the articles and consent forms must be legalized or apostilled, and the notary will certify the due execution of the original articles for the registration file.
required_dossiers: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in 2 originals
Draft notarized articles, if required by the notary
Incorporators' passport or ID copies
Corporate seal (chop) specimen of each incorporator
Apostilled or consular-legalized signature pages for non-resident incorporators
Power of attorney to local counsel for notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the registry objects to an article clause, amend the conflicting provision by a notarial deed of amendment and have all incorporators re-execute the corrected page. If the object clause is too broad for the court's business-object examination, narrow it to the actual software, telematics, data processing, and consulting services and submit a revised clean copy to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Payment and Stamping of the Contribution Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean licensed commercial bank selected by the incorporators, with foreign exchange dealing authority; in-kind contribution valuations examined under court supervision if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon execution of the articles, the proposed company or the promoters must pay the full cash contribution amount into a dedicated deposit account at a Korean commercial bank. The account may be held in the name of the proposed company, or in the name of a promoter in trust, but the bank must be instructed to issue a deposit certificate or balance certificate addressed to the court registry. If the contribution is made in property other than cash, the in-kind assets must be examined by a court-appointed appraiser or by an expert approved by the court, and a valuation report must be obtained. The subscription ledger must list the name of each member, the number of equity interests subscribed, the contribution payable, the mode of payment, and the date of full payment. After payment, the representative director must sign a statutory confirmation that the whole capital has actually been contributed and that the bank balance certificate is authentic. The bank will keep a copy of the foreign investment report certificate for the inbound remittance.
required_dossiers: Fixed deposit account application or temporary corporate account application
Inbound foreign currency remittance slip or domestic won transfer record
KOTRA foreign investment report certificate or bank confirmation of notification
Subscription ledger of members and subscribed interests
Signed statutory capital contribution confirmation
In-kind asset valuation report, if applicable
Bank balance certificate or deposit certificate addressed to the court
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue a balance certificate in the proposed company name, transfer the funds into a legally compliant subscription deposit account or obtain a corrected certificate naming the proposed company as the beneficial holder. If the in-kind valuation is queried, apply to the court for appointment of an independent appraiser and supplement the registration file with the court-approved valuation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office (or the Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office); electronic filing through the Korean Internet Registration System (www.iros.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After all contribution payments are completed and the articles are finalized, the representative director or court filing agent must submit the incorporation registration application to the competent District Court Registration Office. The filing may be made electronically through the Internet Registration System or physically at the court registry counter. The application must contain the company name, the registered office exact address, the business purpose, the total capital contribution units, the names and resident identification of the directors and auditor, and the representative director's authority. The registration officer will verify that the articles, the contribution payment confirmation, the lessor's consent, and the powers of attorney are complete, and will verify the promptness of the filing. Upon approval, the court enters the company in the commercial registry and issues a certified copy of the corporate registration extract. The applicant must pay the registration license tax and court fee at the time of filing. A separate business registration with the National Tax Service must be made after court registration.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate registration application form
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit and balance certificate proving full contribution payment
Subscription ledger and statutory payment confirmation
Lessor's written consent to use the registered office and address proof
Power of attorney to the local filing agent and identification of the representative director
Court registration fees and registration license tax payment confirmation
Foreign investment report certificate, if a non-resident investor is subscribing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order, the filing agent must respond within the statutory period, normally two weeks, by submitting the corrected form or additional evidence. If the registration is refused, the company may refile immediately after correcting the defect or file an immediate appeal under the Korean Non-Contentious Case Registration Procedure Act. During the suspension period, the company should not execute contracts requiring corporate standing unless the counterparty accepts the pending registration status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Tax Registration, Corporate Seal Registration, and Foreign-Invested Enterprise Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district office controlling the registered office address; local notary public for corporate seal registration; KOTRA for foreign-invested enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court issues the certified corporate registration extract, the company must apply for a business registration certificate at the National Tax Service district office controlling the registered office address, using the court-issued registration extract as the primary legal document. The company must also register its corporate seal with a notary public to obtain a corporate seal certificate, which is essential for signing bank mandates, commercial contracts, and annual filings. If the company qualifies under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the representative director must obtain the foreign-invested enterprise registration certificate from KOTRA within the notification period to preserve tax benefits and exchange-transaction advantages. The company should also apply for an e-Tax account, VAT invoice issuance credentials, and any relevant electronic payment merchant documentation for Stripe Billing or wire-transfer banking. This final step closes the formation process and leaves the entity ready for operational licensing assessment.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the corporate registration extract from the court
Corporate seal certificate issued by the notary public
Business registration application form
Lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney for tax filing agent and accountant
Passport and resident identification of representative director
Foreign investment report certificate and KOTRA application for foreign-invested enterprise certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service delays business registration, the court registration extract and provisional tax registration may be used to open bank accounts; if the corporate seal certificate is delayed, obtain a second corporate seal registration at an alternative notary office. If KOTRA rejects the foreign-invested enterprise certificate, file a corrective notification with the original foreign exchange bank and resubmit the KOTRA application with corrected beneficiary and shareholding details.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for the registered digital SaaS scope; the business is ISIC 6201 computer programming activities with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If a physical logistics dispatch center or fleet operations depot is established later, the competent authorities would be the Si/Gun/Gu municipal office under the Building Act and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for commercial vehicle operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for the initial software and telematics SaaS business. Payment settlement through Stripe Billing or bank wire transfer is treated as merchant acceptance, not as a licensed electronic financial business; a separate license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act would be required only if the company eventually holds customers' funds or operates a payment scheme.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable for the initial registered office and software activity; if any future physical facility is planned, the Ministry of Environment and the Korean Environment Corporation (KECO) would be the competent authorities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for the registered scope: no project falls within Schedule 1 or Schedule 2 of the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act, and no building construction or land disturbance is being undertaken.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for the formation stage because there are no point-source wastewater discharges, VOC emission stacks, chemical storage tanks, or hazardous waste generation points. The office will generate only ordinary municipal solid waste, which must be collected by a licensed local waste hauler. If the company later dispatches or operates physical logistics vehicles, the Clean Air Conservation Act emission standards and local air-quality ordinances will apply to the vehicle owner at the operational stage, not to the software formation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to the digital SaaS company formation, but general office compliance is mandatory: the leased office must have valid fire-fighting and evacuation certification under the Fire Services Act, the building owner must maintain a multiple-occupancy building fire safety certificate, and the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office employees. No civil defense permit, chemical safety clearance, or structural load inspection is required because the company occupies standard office space and does not operate warehouses or industrial premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: Hometax (hometax.go.kr). Customs export filings: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity with no domestic place of business that supplies taxable electronic/digital services in Korea, file a simplified VAT registration application through Hometax or with the competent district tax office through a designated Korean tax representative. Attach certificate of incorporation or foreign registration certificate, articles of association, board resolution appointing the tax representative, power of attorney, identity documents, proof of foreign address, and bank account details; authenticate foreign documents by apostille/consular legalization and Korean translation. Upon approval NTS issues a simplified VAT registration number with a leading 0 prefix. For a foreign entity establishing a Korean branch or domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC, file standard business registration with the competent district tax office before commencing business; the domestic entity receives a 10-digit business registration number which functions as TIN/VAT ID, and the branch may also obtain a corporate customs code via UNI-PASS for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law has no check-the-box election; a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate tax under the Corporate Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary exemption threshold for LLCs; registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply. An optional simplified taxpayer regime applies only to individual small businesses with annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000. For non-resident suppliers of electronic/digital services to Korean consumers, simplified VAT registration is mandatory without de minimis turnover exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) must be issued through Hometax or an NTS-approved ASP within one day after each supply, with real-time or near-real-time transmission to NTS using official API or web service. Export invoices must be reported electronically as zero-rated supplies with customs declaration numbers linked to UNI-PASS data. No physical anti-fraud stamp is required; NTS uses e-invoice database matching, cash receipt reporting for consumer sales above KRW 10,000, and trade data reconciliation to detect fraud.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported from Korea after acceptance of an export declaration by Korea Customs Service, with title/risk transferred offshore and foreign exchange proceeds collected within the statutory settlement period. Qualifying services such as fleet telematics SaaS are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident customer for use wholly outside Korea; the supplier must demonstrate through contracts, technical logs, IP/user evidence, and billing files that the services were not consumed in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (UNI-PASS export clearance certificate)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Korea
Commercial invoice and packing list matching export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and KCS jointly scrutinize zero-rated export records. If export evidence is false or insufficient, zero-rating is denied; NTS assesses 10% VAT on the supply, adds 40% penalty tax for fraudulent underreporting or 20% for negligent underreporting plus daily interest. Criminal liability may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, and false customs declarations are separately sanctioned by Korea Customs Service under the Customs Act, including imprisonment and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the central bank and delegated foreign exchange administrator, with supervisory powers exercised jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea applies a liberalised current-account convertibility regime for residents, meaning that trade-related receipts and payments in foreign currency can generally move through authorised foreign exchange banks after routine documentary verification. The Korean won is convertible for genuine export earnings, service fees, and operational remittances, but capital and financial account transactions, such as foreign direct investment, offshore borrowings, equity subscriptions, and acquisition of foreign financial assets, are not fully frei without prior registration or post-transaction reporting. Inbound capital under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act is routed through Invest KOREA and the designated foreign exchange bank, where the foreign investor obtains a foreign investment registration certificate and the domestic entity receives a capital verification report. Profit repatriation in the form of dividends or liquidation distributions is legally permissible once the foreign capital has been fully registered and the outgoing remittance is supported by an audit-confirmed distributable profit computation, sufficient proof of paid-in capital, and the bank's foreign exchange transaction declaration. Practical hurdles still exist because each conversion and outward remittance must be linked to an original source document, the company's frequently used foreign exchange bank must certify the transaction, and incomplete customer due diligence dossiers, missing source-of-wealth narratives, or inconsistent UBO structures will slow approval and may trigger deferral of the remittance until the bank's anti-money laundering committee is satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its enforcement decree, export proceeds from goods or cross-border services, including logistics software subscriptions and telematics licensing fees, must be collected within one year from the date of the export declaration or the date of service completion, unless the authorised foreign exchange bank approves an extension for long-term contracts or staged deliveries. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio requiring the surrender of export proceeds into Korean won; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a dwelled foreign exchange account or convert it to KRW at the agreed bank rate. However, 100% of the proceeds must flow through an institution licensed in Korea to handle foreign exchange, and any single transaction exceeding the equivalent of USD 50,000 must be reported by the bank to the Bank of Korea through the electronic reporting system within three business days of settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Currency Account / Operational Demand Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs, such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Payoneer, operate with weak or non-existent direct banking charters in South Korea. The Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea do not recognise a foreign EMI as a licensed local bank, and Korean corporate entities are not permitted to use these platforms as their principal treasury bank for payroll, tax remittance, FX settlement, or capital verification. An overseas EMI may be used only as a supplementary collection rail to receive inbound payments from foreign logistics clients, but any such flow must ultimately be swept into a domestic foreign exchange bank account, and the EMI itself must be able to produce complete remittance records and underlying purpose codes. The feasibility rating is therefore Low for primary treasury management and Medium only for lightweight cross-border receivables collection where the amount per transaction is below the reporting threshold.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean tier-1 banks generally require at least one authorised officer or statutory director to appear physically in a Korean branch to execute the account opening mandate and undergo a KYC interview. A foreign director who cannot travel may grant a limited power of attorney with apostilled certification before a notary or the competent consular authority, and the attorney-in-fact must present the original corporate documents, the apostilled formation certificate, a board resolution approving the account opening, passport copies of all beneficial owners, and evidence of the actual business operation. Remote video KYC is not a substitute for the initial branch interview in most domestic banks, although some banks will accept a consular interview performed at the overseas Korean embassy provided the completed attestation is couriered to the branch. For this logistics SaaS entity, the recommended KYC path is for the statutory director to personally attend the branch with a certified English-Korean translation of the corporate contract, proof of physical office or registered agent in Korea, and full UBO declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and watchlist hits are triggered because the logistics client base operates in countries subject to enhanced due diligence, or because telematics data derived from fleet route optimisation could raise export-control concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company must produce a commercially obtained sanctions screening report covering directors, shareholders, and material clients, a list of all jurisdictions in which the SaaS platform operates, and an export-licence determination from the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or the Korea Strategic Trade Institute confirming that no export licence is required for the relevant software and data streams. An end-user and end-use attestation from every flagged counterparty, together with a written data compliance policy compliant with the Personal Information Protection Act and the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilisation, will allow the bank to clear the politically exposed persons and dual-use technology flags.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for inbound foreign direct investment begins with the overseas investor transferring USD or KRW through the SWIFT system to a Korean tier-1 foreign exchange bank using the remittance purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment' or 'Equity Investment' as defined by the Bank of Korea's foreign exchange information system. The Yuhan Hoesa must simultaneously complete the foreign investment registration through Invest KOREA, and after the wire is received the bank will issue a capital verification certificate with a foreign currency purchase slip and deposit the converted KRW into the entity's capital escrow account. The bank then reports the transaction to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System within three business days, and the company's registered capital according to the Korean commercial registry must match the verified amount. No cash contributions, virtual currency, peer-to-peer transfers, or third-party cross-border funding are acceptable; all funds must come from the registered foreign investor's own bank account and be traceable through the formal banking network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine cross-border operating expenditures, such as overseas server hosting, software licence fees, employee reimbursements, and telematics data licensing payments, should be settled through a SWIFT MT103 wire message with the correct current-account foreign exchange purpose code, supported by the relevant invoices and contracts retained for at least five years. Large procurement of hardware for on-premise fleet infrastructure or multiple-year vendor subscriptions should be executed either through a commercial letter of credit opened at a Korean bank in favour of the overseas beneficiary, or through documentary collections (D/P and D/A) issued against the transport documents and commercial invoice. All outbound KRW or foreign-currency payments must be routed through the entity's authorised foreign exchange bank, the bank will file the statutory transaction report to the Bank of Korea, and the company must maintain the underlying trade settlement records in Korean or English to satisfy both the Bank of Korea and the Korea Customs Service if no physical goods are involved.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with licenced Korean foreign exchange banks, valid only when the entity can prove real trade exposure through export invoices, logistics subscription contracts, or future foreign-currency receivables, and limited to the maturity of the underlying exposure.

Offshore USD/KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used by non-resident counterparties only after verification of a genuine hedging need; Korean-resident issuers are generally required to use onshore deliverable forwards and must obtain explicit Bank of Korea permission for any offshore NDF transaction that deviates from the real-trade principle.

Cross-currency swap contracts between KRW and USD for hedging loan principal or interest flows from a foreign shareholder loan, subject to prior approval by the authorised foreign exchange bank and the production of the loan agreement, interest schedule, and financial statements confirming the underlying liability.

Currency options and knock-in forward formats are available for corporates with repeated monthly trade exposure, but each option contract must be individually tied to a forecast export or import invoice and cannot be used for pure speculative treasury gains under Korean FX regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (with audited financial statements attached if subject to external audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the close of the calendar fiscal year; for non-calendar fiscal years, within three months of the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-reporting penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (increasing to 40% for fraudulent omission); overdue daily interest at statutory rates of approximately 0.03% per day for up to 36 months; forced collection measures; persistent non-filing may trigger court ordered dissolution under Article 520-2 of the Korean Commercial Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified CPA audit report (when statutory thresholds are met) submitted to shareholders and regulatory authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year end (April 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to commission the audit or submit the report: directors are subject to imprisonment or fines up to KRW 100 million (approximately USD 74,000); delayed filing attracts administrative penalty surcharges and the authority may compel correction of the deficient filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of members (and registration of any officer changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting within three months of fiscal year end (March 31 for calendar-year companies); officer changes are registered within two weeks after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that fails to hold a general meeting or fails to register director reappointments is subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act (up to KRW 1,000,000, approximately USD 740); persistent failure to register changes can result in court-ordered dissolution for continued non-compliance

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable base exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local corporate income surtax, equating to a 26.4% effective top statutory headline rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME/progressive first bracket rate of 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; existing R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenses; job-creation tax credits; Free Economic Zone licensed enterprises may qualify for up to a 5-year corporate income tax holiday and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years for eligible foreign investment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 10, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement (and associated schedules ER-10, ER-30, ER-50), filed through the National Tax Service HomeTX electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, with semi-annual intermediate corporate tax prepayments for business years exceeding six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the corporation's business year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the filing deadline is 31 March of the following year unless an NTS extension is granted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales and operating revenue from logistics fleet dispatch software subscriptions, telematics data licences, and related professional services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean domestic LLC (Yuhan Hoesa), include worldwide revenue if place of effective management is in Korea. If the Korean vehicle is classified as a branch/permanent establishment of a foreign principal, enter only Korean-source revenue. Arm's-length intercompany revenue from a foreign parent must be supported by a benchmarking analysis; omission of a related-party service invoice triggers transfer pricing examination and allocation of deemed profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible payments for software licences, patents, telematics data access, trademark usage, and similar intangibles paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the payer is the Korean entity and the recipient is a non-resident, such royalties are subject to 22% withholding tax (20% national plus 2% local surtax) unless treaty relief is obtained. The expense may be denied if the intangible had no economic substance in Korea or the beneficial owner of the IP cannot be substantiated. Enter the gross amount and disclose in the cross-border related-party schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory declaration of all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including type, amount, transfer pricing method, and comparability analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule is reportable once reportable intercompany transactions exceed the statutory documentation threshold. Provide separate analyses for fleet dispatch services, software royalties, cost-sharing agreements, management fees, and interest on intercompany loans. Incomplete filing or a Schedule 30 inconsistent with the Local File will expose the taxpayer to a 30% penalty on the estimated adjusted income and a full audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward losses deductible against taxable income under Corporate Tax Act Article 13.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses evidenced by prior timely filed returns may be carried forward for up to 10 years. Loss importation via a merger or an intra-group restructuring is scrutinized under anti-abuse rules; a loss claim lacking audited financial statements or an arm's-length allocation of common overheads is a classic fatal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for income or withholding taxes paid to a foreign jurisdiction on Korean-source or allocated profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident beneficiary receiving dividends from the Korean LLC can claim a foreign tax credit in the resident jurisdiction, but the Korean return must not reduce Korean corporate tax unless the foreign tax was actually paid and arises on the same taxable income. Attach the foreign tax remittance evidence and the competent authority document; an unfounded claim is treated as fraudulent understatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 501 — Non-Resident Shareholder Withholding and Treaty Relief Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of withholding tax on outbound dividends, branch profits, interest, and royalties, including treaty-reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a dividend paid to a foreign shareholder, the Korean LLC must withhold and remit the statutory 22% aggregate WHT unless a tax treaty rate applies. The Schedule must identify the ultimate beneficial owner and attach the Tax Residency Certificate and Form for Treaty Reduced Withholding. Failure to satisfy beneficial ownership substance test converts a valid treaty claim into a criminal red flag.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under Corporate Tax Act Article 66; under-reporting: additional tax of 10% of the understated amount; an intentional fraudulent overstatement can be subject to a 40% understatement penalty. Overdue corporate income tax accrues delinquency interest of 0.025% per day for up to 3 years. A wilfully false return with tax evaded exceeding KRW 30 million may escalate to criminal prosecution with imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory withholding for non-resident dividend recipients (20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income surtax); treaty rates may reduce this to 5% or 15% depending on ownership and DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the beneficial owner must submit, before the distribution date or before the WHT reporting date: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority; (2) Form No. 17 'Application for Income Tax Treaty Reduction/Exemption' filed through HomeTX; (3) a Beneficial Ownership Statement confirming the recipient has actual economic substance, the right to the income stream, and no flow-through shell arrangement; (4) evidence of ownership threshold, e.g. 25% or 10% direct holding, for the dividend article of the relevant treaty. The Korean withholding agent must retain these records for the statute of limitations. If the application is rejected, the 22% tax must be withheld and a refund may be pursued through the NTS international tax office.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 22% aggregate statutory rate (20% national plus 2% local); treaties typically reduce royalties to 10% or 15% for copyrights and technological software. Interest: 22% aggregate statutory rate; treaties usually reduce to 10% or 0% on qualifying financial institutions. Intercompany debt must observe the Korean thin-capitalization rule (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for general companies, 6:1 for financial companies) or excess interest is recharacterized as dividends and denied deduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate intercompany transaction value triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; a consolidated group revenue of KRW 100 billion or more also requires Master File; Country-by-Country Report threshold is KRW 400 billion consolidated revenue. Reportable international transaction Schedule 30 disclosure applies when intercompany transactions exceed KRW 500 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulation like common law free zone jurisdictions. Instead, the Corporate Tax Act applies the 'head office/place of effective management' test to determine domestic corporate status. For the Korean LLC to be treated as fully taxable in Korea, strategic management, the board of directors' meetings, treasury decisions, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) for software development, fleet data analytics, contract negotiation, and risk management must actually be performed in Korea. A pass-through Yuhan Hoesa with no locally maintained employees, no premises, or no operative substance will be challenged on substance-over-form doctrine, its payments to offshore affiliates will be disallowed, and CFC rules may attribute profits to Korean controlling shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Abusive Royalty/Gross Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording annual royalty service fees to a Singapore or Cayman affiliate that owns no workforce and performs no development, marketing, or route-dispatch functions, thereby deducting artificial intangible charges from the Korean tax base and suppressing domestic profit; also failing to withhold 22% on the paid royalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 15, 26, 35 and Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3: unlawful tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and/or a fine of up to 30 times the evaded tax; tax adjustment assessment with a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty under CIT Act Article 66, plus daily delinquency interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean Commercial Act Article 401(3) permits creditors and tax authorities to pierce the corporate veil and demand personal compensation from directors who knowingly authorized false expenses. The director may be named a 'representative taxpayer' under the National Tax Collection Act and subject to asset seizure, travel restriction (overseas departure ban or blacklisting), and criminal indictment for joint principal tax evasion with exposure to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Omission of Cross-Border Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Schedule 30 or maintain the arm's-length documentation, Local File, and Master File when the aggregate related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 10 billion; alternatively, submitting a Local File whose tested-party analysis and functional profile contradict the information reported on the Corporate Tax Return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Article 12-2 and Article 12-13 authorize the NTS to reject the reported price and estimate a commensurate arm's-length income; a 30% additional tax and up to KRW 100 million penalty may be imposed for deliberate non-submission. If the intercompany transaction is a financing arrangement, thin-capitalization penalties of 20% of deemed under-distribution apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director or representative who knowingly fails to disclose cross-border transactions is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate income tax plus surcharges; NTS may revoke the company's business registration, enforce a departure ban on the director, and pursue criminal penalties under the Act on Aggravated Punishment for Specific Economic Offences if the scale of tax under-reporting exceeds KRW 100 million, with imprisonment of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and AML/Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee or conduit shareholder in a tax haven jurisdiction to hold the Korean LLC's equity for the benefit of a Korean resident, misleading beneficial ownership analysis, circumventing foreign exchange reporting obligations, and filing false withholding treaty forms to obtain a reduced DTA rate on dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 17 and Financial Information Act (AML) impose administrative fines and criminal punishment of up to 3 years' imprisonment for unregistered beneficial ownership and false reporting. The withholding agent is liable for the 22% WHT not withheld, plus an additional tax of up to 50% under the Corporate Tax Act Article 67-2 for failure to withhold tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in nominee-barrier structuring are personally accountable for the unpaid withholding tax, civil damages to the Korean Revenue, and criminal complicity in AML fraud. A court may lift the corporate veil under Commercial Act Article 388 and the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 12-2, leaving the director's personal bank accounts, vehicles, and fleet assets in the name of family trusts as attachable. Those involved may also be placed on the NTS criminal blacklist, subjected to immigration departure prevention, and, upon conviction, sentenced to imprisonment for up to 7 years for aggravated tax fraud.
